pw_slow_hash.evidence: server.py:79-81 salt = secrets.token_bytes(16) ... hashlib.scrypt(password.encode(), salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)
pw_slow_hash.note: scrypt with a random 16-byte salt; verified with hmac.compare_digest at server.py:92

token_csprng.note: Random 256-bit opaque token; only its SHA-256 hash is stored (server.py:271)

no_hardcoded_secret.note: Tokens are random and not signed, so there is no signing key. No literal secrets appear in the source; the env defaults (PORT, HOST, CORS_ORIGIN at server.py:21-23) are not secrets.

token_expiry.evidence: server.py:169 SELECT user_id FROM sessions WHERE token_hash = ?
token_expiry.note: sessions.created_at is stored (server.py:61), but auth_user never checks token age, so tokens stay valid forever

logout_revokes.note: Logout only clears client storage. The server has no logout route and never deletes from sessions.

owner_checks.evidence: server.py:226 WHERE id=? AND user_id=?; server.py:319 UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND user_id=?; server.py:337 DELETE FROM notes WHERE id=? AND user_id=?; server.py:291 SELECT id FROM notes WHERE id=? AND user_id=?
owner_checks.note: Read, update, delete and share are all limited to the owner

share_token_strong.note: 256 bits from a cryptographic RNG; only the hash is stored

login_rate_limit.evidence: server.py:237 if path in ("/api/signup", "/api/login") and not limited(ip + ":auth"): self.error(429, ...)
login_rate_limit.note: Limits each IP to 12 attempts per 60 s (server.py:101) and counts all attempts, not just failures. The counter is in memory and per IP only.

sql_parameterized.note: Every query with user input uses ? placeholders (lines 169, 204, 216, 226, 255, 265, 271, 284, 291, 296, 319, 337)

xss_safe_render.note: Titles and bodies are always set as text. innerHTML is used only for fixed markup and the server-generated share token (index.html:27).

security_headers.evidence: server.py:126-130 X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; X-Frame-Options: DENY; Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; ... script-src 'self'
security_headers.note: headers_common() is called on every response from reply(). Side effect: script-src 'self' blocks the inline scripts in both HTML pages, so the frontend would not run as served.
